slice.objective: Identify one recent autonomous-science mechanism that can reduce proprietary frontier-model dependence while preserving inspectable evidence for research-problem formulation.

public_sources.title: SGHA: Evidence-Grounded Research Problem Discovery with Local Language Models

observations: SGHA is presented as a fully automated corpus-first research-problem discovery system whose LLM components run on a locally served open-weight 9B model rather than proprietary frontier-model APIs.

Its mechanism structures a literature corpus into evidence-linked paper objects and a typed evidence graph, detects unresolved structural patterns, screens candidate gaps before formulation, and emits traceable problem families with assumptions, objectives, success criteria, and remaining ambiguities.

The authors compare SGHA with the AI Scientist-v2 idea-formulation module across five machine-learning domains and report that evidence-constrained local-model reasoning can produce promising, inspectable research-problem formulations without frontier-model use during generation or verification.
inferences: For this role's Phase-1 objective, the transferable mechanism is not 'use a smaller model' alone; it is corpus-first structuralization plus typed evidence constraints, which can shift part of scientist-agent ideation from opaque parametric recall toward auditable retrieval-and-graph reasoning.
This mechanism is a plausible candidate for reducing dependence on finite proprietary-model quota in the problem-formulation stage while preserving explicit provenance and uncertainty fields.
uncertainties: The abstract does not establish parity with frontier models on a universal scientist-agent benchmark, nor does it establish zero total compute or zero infrastructure cost.

The reported comparison is limited to five machine-learning domains and to research-problem formulation; it does not by itself validate downstream experiment execution, recovery, manuscript generation, or end-to-end scientific correctness.
No Phase-1 closure claim follows from this slice; integration value must be tested under the repository's existing zero-Work, zero-finite-quota, zero-incremental-cost gates.
slice.bounded_result: Candidate mechanism recorded: local open-weight 9B + corpus-first typed evidence graph + pre-formulation gap screening. Highest-value next test is to check whether an existing clean, already-available local/corpus path can instantiate the evidence-graph formulation step without new paid or finite-quota dependencies, and if so compare traceability/quality against the current clean scientist-agents baseline on one bounded topic.

continuation: Read only this role's current clean state/config plus public primary sources; test one bounded topic for whether corpus-first typed evidence-graph formulation can be instantiated using already-authorized zero-incremental-cost resources, record exact provenance and failure conditions, and do not consume O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, or shared-ledger semantics.
